title: VBR resultant force during upper-body flexion while standing (points A/B/C), per patient
subcategory: VBR resultant force vs trunk inclination, standing flexion
condition: in vivo, VBR + posterior fixator, >6 months post-op

quantity.name: resultant force on VBR
quantity.definition: ABSOLUTE resultant force (geometric sum of Fx, Fy, Fz) on the telemeterised VBR at three time points of a standing forward-flexion trial: A = onset of force plateau, B = maximal trunk inclination, C = maximal force during return to upright. Per patient median and range over trials (Fig 2b); trunk inclination at the same points from Fig 2a (angle between vertical and a line fitted to the back over lumbar/lower thoracic spine).

source.authors: Dreischarf M, Albiol L, Zander T, Arshad R, Graichen F, Bergmann G, Schmidt H, Rohlmann A
source.n: 5 patients (4 M, 1 F) with telemeterised VBR (WP1-WP4 at L1, WP5 at L3); 135 trials (82 standing, 53 sitting) from 37 sessions
source.sample: in vivo, patients with A3 compression fracture treated with posterior internal fixator + telemeterised vertebral body replacement; only sessions >6 months post-op (up to 65 months)
source.age: WP1 62, WP2 71, WP3 69, WP4 63, WP5 66 y (at surgery)

protocol.summary: Standing forward flexion of the upper body with hands kept close to the legs and arms hanging; no speed instructions; 1-2 repetitions per session; sessions >6 months post-op. Trials with the characteristic plateau pattern (~90%) analysed at points A/B/C. Trunk inclination from video.
how_to_simulate: Model the patient (Table 1 anthropometry) standing upright, arms hanging, then flex the trunk forward with hands close to the legs to the reported inclination angles (A ~33 deg, B ~53 deg, C ~42 deg; per-patient angles in data rows)
Output the resultant (compressive+shear) force at the implant level (L1 for WP1-WP4, L3 for WP5) at each angle

A whole-spine MSK model outputs total segment compression at the implant level, not the implant share; compare trends/relative changes unless the model includes the VBR and posterior fixator; e.g. compare the plateau shape (force at B ~ force at A) and the force increase vs upright (see dreischarf2015.flexion_force_increase_standing_vs_sitting)

subject_model.implant_note: VBR replaces parts of the fractured vertebral body and the adjacent discs; posterior internal fixator remains in situ
subject_model.source: Dreischarf 2015 Table 1 (sex, age, height, body mass, BMI, fractured vertebra, fixator levels, implantation date)

protocol.notes: Load measured on a telemeterised vertebral body replacement (modified Synex, 6 load components, accuracy ~2% force / 5% moment of 3000 N / 20 Nm calibration range) that shares the load with the posterior internal fixator, residual vertebral bone and bone graft; the VBR force is NOT the total spinal load. Text (Results): angle at A on average 33 deg (range of patient medians 32-39 deg); B on average 53 deg (44-66 deg); force at A and B approximately 450 N on average (range 425-638 N); maximal force C on average 565 N (450-770 N). About 90% of standing trials showed the plateau pattern; only those trials are in Fig 2 (n per patient differs from Fig 3).

pass_rule.rule: per patient: model within the patient min-max range; group: model within range of patient medians (A,B ~425-640 N; C ~445-770 N) - only if the model includes the VBR/fixator load sharing, otherwise compare shape (plateau between A and B)
